scope: Proposition 21.1 (Scalar solution operator) of the manuscript “Boundary graph deformations for the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Boundary-graph-deformations-for-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4205f51d8f1b130b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 142. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every Z ∈ C1,α(ΩR) and every homotopy parameter s, the trace equation with its assigned constant Dirichlet values has a unique solution f = fs[Z] ∈ C3,α(ΩR). No lower bound on t = t(Z, grad f) is assumed. On bounded sets of trial inputs, these solutions have bounded C3,α norms, uniformly in s. The map (s, Z) 7→ fs[Z] is continuous into C3,α and is locally obtained by inversion of the scalar Dirichlet operator.
